### Added

- **Groups**: name the displays and computers you use together. With two PCs, a Mac and several displays, they rarely all move at once — the ones on a single desk go together, the ones in another room do not. Settings → Groups creates them, a row of groups then appears above the switch centre, and choosing one narrows the switch centre, the host switcher window and the tray menu to what it covers.

  Ticking nothing in either half covers all of that half, so "the two machines at this desk" needs no display list. Groups stay on the computer that made them and are never shared with paired hosts: which displays and computers belong together depends on where a computer sits, and a grouping pushed from elsewhere would be right for neither end. Removing a display from sharing, or unpairing a host, takes it out of every group — the group itself stays, because being emptied is not you deleting it.

- **A crash now says why**: an internal error is written down, with its backtrace, before the app stops. It goes alongside the ordinary log once logging has started (`muxsu-panic.log`), and in the system temp folder before then. The file travels with a diagnostic report too.

### Fixed

- **Windows: the app vanished a few seconds after opening**: the main window appeared, the whole process then disappeared, and the event log held nothing but a bare `0xc0000409` — no log anywhere said why. Tauri builds every window in its configuration before it calls MuxSU's own startup routine, and a window starts loading and asking the backend for data as soon as it is built, while the shared state those requests need did not exist yet. All three windows are now built by the startup routine, after that state is in place.

- **After a restart a computer advertised its machine name again**: a rename updated the advertised record at the moment it was made and no later, so starting up again went back to the system's machine name — on macOS the hostname, ending in `.local` — and never corrected itself. A host that has not paired with this one has nothing but that record to go by, so it listed the computer under a name its user had already replaced. Startup now follows the same rule a rename does: the name you chose when there is one, the machine name otherwise.

This version speaks the same protocol as v0.8.2 and pairs and switches with it directly. Groups change nothing about switching itself — only which displays and computers each screen shows.

### Known limitations

- Groups are new in this release and have not been lived with across many setups yet. If the layout or behaviour is not what you expect, Settings → Groups can delete a group at any time, which goes back to showing everything.
- The macOS DMG is ad-hoc signed and not notarized with an Apple Developer ID, so Gatekeeper may ask for it to be allowed by hand.
